1	# WP-003: Repository Manager `updateCredential()` Method
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Extend the Git credentials system from a single-token-per-host model to a multi-credential model with per-repository credential association, auto-selection for single-match hosts, and clear error surfacing for missing credentials.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Add a dedicated `updateCredential()` method to `RepositoryManager` that sets or clears the `CredentialId` field on a repository. This provides the persistence layer for per-repository credential association.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/models/repository/repository.manager.ts` — new `updateCredential()` method
    14	- `src/tests/repository.manager.test.ts` — tests for the new method
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `updateCredential(id: string, credentialId: string | null): Repository` method on `RepositoryManager`
    19	- Unit tests verifying set and clear operations persist correctly
    20	
    21	## Dependencies
    22	
    23	- WP-001
    24	
    25	## Acceptance Criteria
    26	
    27	1. `RepositoryManager.updateCredential(id, credentialId)` sets the `CredentialId` field on the specified repository and persists it to `repositories.json`.
    28	2. `RepositoryManager.updateCredential(id, null)` clears (removes) the `CredentialId` field from the specified repository and persists the change.
    29	3. Calling `updateCredential()` with a non-existent repository ID throws an appropriate error.
    30	4. Unit tests in `src/tests/repository.manager.test.ts` cover set, clear, and invalid-ID scenarios.

    42	The `update()` method signature on `RepositoryManager` stays unchanged — `CredentialId` changes go through this new dedicated method. Depends on WP-001 for the `CredentialId` type on `Repository`.
